A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same focal-diversity ensemble framework despite retitling and substantive revision. All text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v2's Appendices A–G; v1 has no appendix. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark accuracies, training curves, cost analysis and aligned-model selection results in Tables 1–3 and Figure 3.

after.justification: V2 reports revised benchmark results and additional routing comparisons, ablations, sensitivity experiments, scalability measurements and case studies, including in its appendices.

M1.justification: V1 describes separate REINFORCE/PPO updates. V2 introduces MAPPO with a centralized critic, shared advantage estimation and a critic loss, and adds reward history to the Fusion Agent's observations (Sections 3.2–3.3; Appendix C). These change the learning architecture and inputs beyond renaming MARL-Focal and the Aggregator Agent.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, GSM8K, BBH, MUSR and GPQA, and retain the Alpaca, BeaverTails and TruthfulQA alignment experiments. The latter move to Appendix D. New ablations, model configurations and examples use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds six individual-model comparators in Table 1, including Phi-4-14b, Qwen-2.5-72b and Llama-3-70b. It newly evaluates RouteLLM with three GPQA model pairings (Table 2) and two greedy selection approaches (Figure 4). The original ensemble comparators in Table 3 remain.

E3.justification: V2 reports an expanded benchmark model pool and introduces controlled diversity-metric, branching, hyperparameter and replicated-pool experiments. Its precise pool size is inconsistent: the text says 12 models, while Table 1 lists 14 with reused IDs. The original data splits, ten-pass GSM8K processing and listed default hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds diversity-metric and no-selection controls, branching ablations, consensus and error-correction analyses, hyperparameter sensitivity, replicated-pool scalability and worked examples (Figures 3–6; Appendices B, E and F). These substantially extend v1's training-curve and efficiency analyses. V1's MMLU cost–accuracy scatter is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions show training-curve standard deviations over five experiments. V2 additionally reports mean and standard error over five runs for its main benchmark results and specifies that base-model outputs are fixed across runs. This expands uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in run count.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the proposed method's results across all five benchmarks, including MMLU 73.24 to 77.98 and BBH 49.04 to 65.00. These accompany method and pool changes, so they are not matched-setting gains. V2 also adds numerous comparison, ablation and cost results; v1's alignment results remain unchanged as v2 Table 6.

T1.justification: V2 replaces the MDP formulation with a DEC-POMDP specification and adds centralized-critic, advantage-estimation and MAPPO objectives. Appendix G introduces Lipschitz-based robustness bounds, an ensemble robustness argument and a focal-diversity/covariance derivation absent from v1. These are substantive mathematical additions, irrespective of their correctness.

C1.justification: The central claim that two-stage, diversity-guided selection and fusion outperform individual LLMs remains. V2 refines the claimed formulation to DEC-POMDP, changes the advertised improvement from 5.51% to 8.48%, and foregrounds theoretical robustness support. The retained helpfulness, safety and truthfulness application is no longer emphasized in the conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly assumes temporally related queries with infrequent task switches, explains centralized-critic stabilization, and discusses discount-factor nonconvergence and nonmonotonic cost versus pool size. Appendices E–F additionally discuss unavailable API logits and cases where fusion succeeds despite incorrect component predictions. These materially expand mechanisms, limitations and applicability conditions.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents unshuffled question ordering, MCQ probability extraction, grid-search selection, H100 hardware, parameter counts, training/inference times and API pricing. It provides expanded offline and online pseudocode and states that per-task LLM outputs are available through the existing repository. The repository URL itself is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds substantive positioning against recent RL ensemble approaches by Chakraborty et al. and Fu et al., contrasting fixed-size ensembles with dynamic subset selection. It also contrasts online exploration with offline genetic pruning and adds MAPPO and theoretical references. This revises v1's broad first-approach positioning for RL-based pruning and generation.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the introduction and methodology, integrates related work into the introduction, and combines problem formulation with design. Dataset details, alignment experiments and cost discussion move into organized appendices. The title, method name, agent terminology and author list also change.

P2.justification: V2 switches from two-column to single-column presentation, redraws Figure 1 around the centralized critic, rearranges the retained Figure 2 surfaces and changes Figure 3's panels. It adds multiple analysis figures and tables, expands Table 1's structure and relocates the alignment table to Appendix D.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful component ablations, sensitivity analyses, uncertainty reporting and implementation details missing from v1. However, its model-pool description conflicts with Table 1, and the new Appendix G.2 conditions on the focal error indicator being constant yet concludes covariance of -1; that covariance must instead be zero. The added empirical and documentation benefits coexist with unreliable new theoretical support and experimental ambiguity, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
